facts.fact: The national agency ANRPTS said the Houwiyeti app began operating on 2 January 2024 and lets citizens issue a digital identity and verify its validity, and public and private bodies can verify QR-coded digital civil-status extracts through the app's verification service.

The national agency ANRPTS said citizens can issue a digital identity and verify its validity in the Houwiyeti mobile app, available on Google Play from 2 January 2024, though passport, ID-card and residence-card services stay blocked pending regulatory texts.

systems.platform: mobile app (Google Play; App Store pending)

MRT.note: No records passing between the civil register and the ID system are stated.
The app orders and verifies civil-status extracts; it does not say births or deaths are registered digitally.
No enrolment count or share is stated.
No number at birth is stated.
Nothing on who builds, operates or owns the system.
No register keyed on the ID number is stated.

facts.fact: The agency ANRPTS said the Houwiyeti system began operating on 2 January 2024, letting citizens and resident foreigners open an account and issue a digital identity, while ID-card services stay blocked until regulatory texts are aligned.

MRT.note: The agency is named for the population register but the document does not say a register is in service.
The app serves extracts and tracking; no digital entry of events at local offices is stated.
